backlog.spec: Add a small local correction on top of the current pipeline. First compute out-of-fold predictions for the training set with a 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by Murcko scaffold, using exactly the existing model (ridge base plus two-stage XGBoost), and form training residuals r_i = y_i - oof_pred_i. Then, for every test molecule, find its 5 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) and compute a similarity-weighted mean of their residuals, with weights equal to the similarity raised to the fourth power. Add 0.5 times that weighted residual mean to the model's prediction, but only when the top similarity is at least 0.5; otherwise add nothing. Keep everything else unchanged. This targets systematic local bias in regions where the global model is consistently off.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour residual correction

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into five groups with sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold using the Murcko scaffold SMILES (from rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) as the group label, so internal validation mirrors the outer protocol. For each candidate stage-2 round count in 200, 400, 800 and 1600, compute the mean out-of-fold MAE of the full pipeline, choose the best count, then refit on all training rows with that count and predict the test set. Everything else stays as it is. This replaces a fixed guess with a per-fold choice at the cost of about five extra fits.
backlog.title: Pick the stage-2 round count by internal scaffold-grouped validation

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, after building Xtr and Xte, derive a column mask using training data only: keep a column if it is non-zero in at least five training molecules and its training variance is above zero. Apply the same mask to Xtr and Xte before fitting the boosting stages. Everything else is unchanged. With roughly 580 training rows per fold, most of the 2048 Morgan bits are near-empty, and removing them shrinks the space the column-subsampling draws from so each tree sees more informative candidate splits.
backlog.title: Prune rare and constant feature columns inside each fit

backlog.spec: Wrap the existing XGBoost two-stage residual fit in a loop over five seeds derived deterministically from the seed argument (for example seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4, used as random_state for both stages). Keep the physchem ridge base fitted once outside the loop and keep all features and hyperparameters identical to the current script; only the XGBoost random_state changes between members. Average the five residual predictions (plain mean) and add the ridge base prediction to get the final output. Nothing else changes. With subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3 the individual fits are noticeably stochastic, so seed averaging should remove part of the model variance; five fits of 600 total rounds on 728 rows is still fast enough for 15 folds inside ten minutes.
backlog.title: Average the two-stage model over five seeds

backlog.spec: Keep the existing pipeline intact (Ridge baseline, two-stage XGBoost on the residual y minus base_tr). Add a second residual learner: CatBoostRegressor on the same training matrix and the same residual target with loss_function='MAE', iterations=1500, learning_rate=0.03, depth=6, rsm=0.1, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0. Final prediction is base_te plus the equal-weight average of the XGBoost stage-2 prediction and the CatBoost prediction. Import CatBoostRegressor from catboost at the top of the file.
backlog.title: Blend a CatBoost MAE residual model with the XGBoost one

backlog.spec: Keep the current architecture exactly (physchem ridge base, then XGBoost fitting the ridge residuals in two stages: squared-error rounds followed by absoluteerror rounds continued from the first booster). Change only the boosting budget: set learning_rate=0.02 for both stages, stage1 n_estimators=300 with objective reg:squarederror, and stage2 n_estimators=900 with objective reg:absoluteerror continued via xgb_model=stage1.get_booster(). Leave max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8 unchanged. The point is that the L2 warm start may need more rounds and a slower rate once the L1 phase is long; total wall time should stay well under the limit since each fit is only a few hundred shallow trees on 728 rows.
backlog.title: Retune the two-stage round split and learning rate

backlog.spec: Keep the architecture and features exactly as they are and only change the shared params dict and the tree counts. Set max_depth to 4, learning_rate to 0.015, subsample to 0.7, colsample_bytree to 0.2, min_child_weight to 5, and add reg_lambda=2.0. Raise the stage-1 squared-error round count to 400 and the stage-2 absolute-error round count to 1200 so the total shrinkage budget is comparable. With under 600 training rows and thousands of columns, depth 6 trees at learning rate 0.03 are likely overfitting scaffold-held-out folds.
backlog.title: Tune the boosting hyperparameters toward a shallower, slower fit

backlog.spec: Enrich only the linear physchem base, which currently uses TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds and the aromatic-atom fraction. Append to that vector: counts of carboxylic acid, primary/secondary/tertiary amine, sulfonamide and phenol groups via RDKit SMARTS matches; the formal-charge counts of positively and negatively charged atoms; Descriptors.NumHeteroatoms; Descriptors.FractionCSP3; Descriptors.LabuteASA; and Descriptors.MolMR. Standardize the enlarged vector with the same StandardScaler and fit the same Ridge(alpha=1.0); the XGBoost two-stage model keeps fitting the residuals of this base on the unchanged Morgan-plus-descriptor features. Ionization state is the main physical driver of passive permeability, so making it explicit and linear should give the booster cleaner residuals to learn.
backlog.title: Ionization and polarity descriptors in the ridge base

backlog.spec: Add a third predictor alongside the current pipeline: build binary Morgan bit vectors (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test, compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between train and train and between test and train with numpy (intersection over union of the binary matrices), and fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the train-train similarity matrix against the raw target y. Predict on the test-train matrix. Final output is 0.7 times the current prediction plus 0.3 times this similarity-based prediction. Similarity models extrapolate differently from trees on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Stack a fingerprint-similarity kernel ridge model into the ensemble

backlog.spec: Train the whole existing pipeline on a rank-Gaussian version of the target and invert the transform at prediction time. Fit a sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(200, n_train), random_state=seed) on train_y reshaped to a column, transform the targets, run the current ridge base plus two-stage XGBoost residual model on the transformed targets exactly as now, then apply inverse_transform to the test predictions before returning them. Clip the transformed-space predictions to the min and max of the transformed training targets before inverting, so the inverse mapping stays inside the fitted support. Keep features and all hyperparameters unchanged. A Gaussianized target makes the squared-error warm-up stage better behaved if the raw permeability values are skewed or have heavy tails.
backlog.title: Rank-Gaussian target transform with inverse mapping

memo: Helped: swapping RF for XGBoost with L1 loss (0.3828, -0.0589 vs the 0.4417 start). Adding a ridge on six RDKit physchem descriptors plus aromatic-atom features, with XGB fitting its residuals, gave 0.3755/0.3715. A two-stage XGB residual fit (200 rounds of squared-error, then L1) is the current incumbent at 0.3658/0.3652 over 2 runs. Noise-level or no gain (noise sd about 0.0037): bagged XGB 0.3793, 6-model ensemble 0.3795, winsorized targets 0.3727, Avalon+ErG 0.3710, LightGBM, CatBoost, GP, MLP, Tanimoto kernel ridge, MACCS, 3D shape, calibration, quantile correction, polynomial or sparse-L1 ridge bases. Tree and Morgan tuning looks saturated. Next: vary the two-stage recipe (round counts, learning rate, Huber loss for stage two), combine small gains with it (bagging, Avalon/ErG, winsorizing), and add polarity/ionization descriptors (TPSA, HBD, charge) to the ridge. Avoid specs that abort at the engine.
